design: Defect 1 (settle offset): the gate's top check now subtracts the renderer's 6 px entrance lift, so the band's highest point during the first six frames must still clear the three-line seat. Effect: a three-line cue at size 44 is refused (band top 1238.6 would become 1232.6, above the seat at 1238.6); size 42 (h 175.0, lift included 181.0 at most 182.36) is still approved. captionLayout only emits three-line sizes 44, 42 and 40, so 44 is the only size this refuses. Two-line bands are never affected because their height cannot reach the three-line seat with the lift. The renderer was not changed; the lift is a copy of its -6 in the gate, and the test regex-pins the gate constant to the renderer's settle range in DispatchOverlays.tsx. Defect 2 (template): the gate learns the template from board.cinematic_template, the same top-level key Dispatch.tsx reads for routing. A cue declaring max_lines 3 on alloy-loop-v1 is refused with a message naming the template. Undeclared cues on alloy keep their verdict. No change to AlloyLoopEpisode.tsx, editorial.ts or DispatchOverlays.tsx. Controls were recorded from the HEAD gate before editing and the repaired gate's --report output matches them byte for byte.

limits: Not committed or pushed; both files are uncommitted in the working tree. The alloy-loop-v1 fix refuses only declared max_lines 3. The gate still does not validate alloy's own 850 px and size 34 wrap, so an undeclared cue that alloy wraps to three lines (or that slice(0,3) truncates) is still approved, and AlloyLoopEpisode's panel geometry, which draws its third line about 10 px below the panel, is untouched. CAPTION_IGNORES_MAX_LINES is a hand-kept list of one template, so any future template with the same renderer must be added to it. The 6 px lift is duplicated rather than imported because type_fit_probe.tsx is outside the allowed files; the test's regex pin catches drift only while the renderer keeps the literal form interpolate(..., [0, 6], [-N, 0]). Production boards were not inspected, so any shipped board that declares three lines at 44 on any template would now be refused. The test writes its temp boards with mkdtemp under os.tmpdir(), following the gate's own convention, and removes them. The scratch exploration files were written to the session scratchpad. The alloy mutation stands in for the old gate by running the current gate on the board without the template key, which the old gate never read; the revert check ran the real HEAD gate and confirmed both repaired results fail.
